content.text: During a Fourth-of-July storm, Amy, frightened by the thunder, sought Maggie’s lighted room, then went to Mrs. Clifford’s room and later the sitting-room, where Webb comforted her. Webb secretly loves Amy, while Burt courts both Amy and Gertrude Hargrove. After Burt saves Gertrude from a rattlesnake in the mountains, he confesses his love to Amy, who releases him; he then proposes to Gertrude, who accepts. Webb patiently wins Amy’s heart under the mistletoe, and they become engaged. Christmas brings reconciliation, charitable visits to Lumley’s improved home and Alvord’s lonely dwelling, and family happiness. The appended historical section recounts Grant’s 1863 Vicksburg campaign: Federal forces crossed the Mississippi, captured Jackson and Champion’s Hill, besieged Vicksburg, and forced its July 4 surrender; Port Hudson fell soon afterward, giving the Union control of the Mississippi.
